body:
Hi, thank you for the report! Unfortunately the logs don't seem to report anything about `wl_data_offer`, which is the object type responsible for clipboard data handling. I'm afraid that I might need more of it.

If that makes you feel more comfortable, you can send me the full file (or other pieces of it) privately by contacting me on RocketChat :D

This has happened to me a couple of times (very rare) when using a debug version of 4.4.1 (build from repo locally) on Windows 10. But I haven't investigated anything, just restarted the editor. When it happened I couldn't copy any text from Godot's code editor.
Not sure if my comment is helpful. Just adding my 2 cents.

Whoops, I mainly wanted to avoid dumping a 1.5M line file here, but I just searched for `wl_data_offer`, and I got 23 results, some up to line 63k, and the rest from around 1395k up, so here's a more complete version only skipping the million-and-some lines in-between.

[clipboard_take2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21972733/clipboard_take2.zip)

Thanks to the verbose output of the above patch, a chance glance to the output panel while selecting some code had me notice the primary selection message `Couldn't set primary selection, wl_seat#%d doesn't have wp_primary_selection_device.`, and sure enough, <kbd>Ctrl + C</kbd> also stopped working at that point.

So here's the new debug log, I didn't remove anything this time, so its ~770k lines.

[clipboard_v3.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22038734/clipboard_v3.zip)

Mhhh, I've investigated for a while but I'm still completely baffled 💀

I asked you to add those print statements cause I thought that there might have been multiple seat objects but it does not look like it. The "Initializing ... for seat X" messages seem to not be called multiple times either (although that's weird on its own since you run both the project manager and the editor so it should initialize at least twice overall).

The weirdest thing is that the data device just... magically disappears? It's not like the state is invalid, no, there's a basic check for that too.

Perhaps it might be memory corruption? That would be even weirder since the data devices are in the middle of the seat state struct and nothing else seems to be affected.

The only place that explicitly clobbers the data devices is the `global_remove` handler, which never got called.

Would you be comfortable opening the editor with GDB and adding a breakpoint to the "device missing" print statement and generating a core? I think that even just calling `p *ss` and sending me the result should work but given the rarity of the issue I'd advise to generate the core file just in case so that you don't have to wait a few days all the time. I've never done that but according to the docs all it takes is to call `generate-core-file path/to/output/file` during the breakpoint: https://sourceware.org/gdb/current/onlinedocs/gdb.html/Core-File-Generation.html

I'd also recommend opening the project directly instead of going through the project manager, as that avoids mixing the project manager with the editor:

```
WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 path/to/godot --verbose path/to/project.godot
```

with GDB that'd be:

```
WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 gdb --args path/to/godot --verbose path/to/project.godot
```

Thank you for your patience :D

The sadness of getting "good results" sometimes :)

I'm running Manjaro on KDE Plasma 6.3.6 (upgraded from Plasma 5 X11 when Plasma 6 was made available). With regards to I/O peripherals, I typically only have my headphones and microphone plugged in, sometimes my XBox controller, and that's about it, I plug other devices in/out as needed, and I'm pretty sure that when I generated the core file, I had nothing else plugged in.

Here's the output of `wayland-info`: [wayland-info.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22175166/wayland-info.txt)
I'm only seeing a single `wl_seat` in there.

And thank you again for taking the time to investigate this!

Yea wayland-info is fine here.

I think it's time to bring out the big guns. I'll soon™ set up a Manjaro VM and look around. I still have some theories on the possible kind of fault happening here, as each log you sent had some things missing and I have to figure out why.

I'll update you when I find out more.

I was getting the same bug but strangely restarting the editor multiple times (manually or with "Reload Current Project") wasn't enough for me.
I had to close and reopen the terminal (Konsole) from where I was executing `./godot.linuxbsd.editor.x86_64` to fix this.
